text:
“…Say what now?”

It was the night when the piano club’s proposal in the to-be-convened student assembly had been brought to the student council. Masachika had been relaxing in his room, only to have suddenly received a call from Yuki, her words leaving him utterly perplexed.

“Like I said,” Yuki reaffirmed, “It really sounds like there’s gonna be some sorta scheme aimed at Alya-san regarding that student assembly thing that came up today, the one between the piano and light music clubs. Just thought I’d let you know.”

Of course, Masachika understood what she was saying. But why did Yuki have such information in the first place, and why was she going out of her way to tell Masachika, who was, by all accounts, a rival candidate?

“Why… are you warning me here?”

“Because, to be honest… it looks like it’s gonna be something that might be more than I can handle by myself,” Yuki answered after a brief pause in response to his frank question.

It was an unusually timid admission that only deepened his perplexity.

“However,” she then raised her voice slightly as she continued, “I’ve got one condition. As payment for the info, I want you, Onii-chan, to promise not to interfere with the informant.”

“And what’s that s’posed to mean?”

“Well, to put it in a nutshell… Ayano’s the one who’s brought me this info, so we don’t want ol’ Onii-chan getting in the way of her spy work, do we now?”

“Ayano? You mean she’s…” Masachika trailed off, recalling how strangely Ayano had been acting lately as he heard Yuki’s explanation.

Ah, could this be what… that’s been about…?

His childhood friend had looked to be carrying something heavy on her mind, after all. Faced with what seemed like the reason behind it, the option of not asking for the details had simply vanished for Masachika.

“…Alright,” he conceded. “So what’s with this info?”

A brief pause then hung in the air for a moment.

“Nonoa-san looks to be betraying Alya-san.”

“…Huh?”

⋆⋅☆⋅⋆

“What… do you mean?”

It was now early the next morning, where in the student council room, Alisa, having heard the warning that Masachika had gotten from Yuki, donned a look of complete bewilderment. Her mind struggled to keep up, and Masachika didn’t seem to fare any better.

“No like, me too… Nonoa betraying you? I don’t get it,” he parroted her confusion. “In any case, what I’ve heard from Yuki is that she’s trying to use Ayano to isolate me and her from coming to the student assembly, and that she’s trying to maneuver things so that you and Ayano would be assigned to counting the votes. There’s apparently supposed to be… some sorta scheme that’ll threaten your position then…”

Even saying it out loud himself didn’t help it make much more sense. In fact, it was probably why Yuki had passed along such information in the first place: for his help in making sense of it all.

“Regarding all of this… How certain is it?” Alisa asked after seriously thinking it over for a moment.

“I can’t imagine Ayano lying here…” yet Masachika’s tone showed he clearly couldn’t give a firm answer. “Her going all the way to spy is surprising, but again… I guess it’s something she might do if it’s for Yuki. Or rather, it sounds like she’s decided she couldn’t get any more info out of Nonoa and turned to Yuki for her judgment; that’s entirely plausible too. Still, there ain’t really much proof that Yuki herself’s being completely honest ’bout the whole thing either…”

The tip had come from a rival candidate, after all, a tip where they were now forced to suspect their own ally, no less. Who to trust, what to believe, or how far to accept any of it? None of it was clear.

And yet…

“My gut’s telling me that… Yuki’s not lying here. That’s what I think,” Masachika concluded, prompting deep lines to form between Alisa’s brows.

It was only natural. Trusting Yuki meant doubting Nonoa. And for Alisa, the sheer emotional strain of suspecting one of her only friends had to be immense.

“…What if we just go straight to Nonoa-san and probe her about it directly?”

“Nope, can’t do that.”

“Why’s that?”

“I promised I wouldn’t interfere with Ayano’s spying on Nonoa. Us messing up with the wrong move here could make her suspect that her scheme’s been leaked.”

“…In other words, you’re saying we have to pretend we don’t know anything, right?”

“That’s how it looks, hm~?”

Even so, facing the student assembly while pretending to know nothing without any prep was utter foolishness. What kind of scheme awaited them? Or rather, was there even a scheme to begin with at all? There was just so much the two didn’t know, but assuming a conspiracy was in play here, they had to come up with some sort of countermeasure.

Yet… with only the knowledge that Alisa was the target, what kind of action could they even take…?

Should I just have Alya skip the student assembly too…? Masachika let that thought float throughout his mind. No, taking our eyes off the whole thing’s dangerous in its own way, huh? And to start with, dodging the matter here only means kicking the problem down the road. Smarter to deal with it now than get blindsided later…

Thinking through it this far, one person connected to this debacle suddenly came to mind.

“Come to think of it…” Masachika uttered.

“What?”

“Ah, no,” yet he quickly shook his head the moment Alisa clung to the words he had let slip from his mouth.

“Tell me. We need any scrap of information we can get right now, no matter how trivial it is.”

“Ngh, hmm…” Masachika hesitated in the face of his partner’s earnest gaze, before reluctantly speaking. “Truth is… Kiryuuin had also said that Nonoa was plotting something for the student assembly…”

“Kiryuuin…? Like, baldi—Sumire-senpai’s cousin?”

“Yeah, that Kiryuuin. Yuusho Kiryuuin.”

Picturing the pretentious schoolmate who’d been doing nothing but pestering him lately, Masachika’s mouth twisted in displeasure.

“Right. Then, let’s ask that Kiryuuin-san about it too,” Alisa said with a swift decision.

“Huuuuh…? Seriously?”

“Why not?”

“No, for starters, it’s like the guy naturally has it out for Nonoa; no way we’re getting anything objective from him here…” Masachika grimaced as if the thought itself offended him, all while Alisa tilted her head slightly with a complicated look.

“I don’t really know him well, but… him aiming to be student council president back in junior high means he’s capable at the very least, right?” she asked.

“Ahhh. Well… he’s a li’l overconfident and doesn’t really care ’bout the means to get what he wants.”

“And if I remember, he had a debate against Sayaka-san and Nonoa-san and lost, if I’m not mistaken?”

“Yep, right.”

“That means, in other words… he knows Nonoa-san as an opponent more than anyone else, doesn’t he?” Alisa reasoned, eliciting a gasp from Masachika. “That sort of instinct—call it intuition, or rather his judgement—might actually be worth trusting, don’t you think?”

“……”

Such a thought had never crossed Masachika’s mind, and all he could do was freeze, eyes wide at Alisa’s unexpected remark.

That’s true… It’s precisely ’cause he’s a villain who’s used to tossin’ malice at others that maybe he’s all the more sensitive to malice directed at himself, he rationalized. Could that… actually be it? But, man…

Nevertheless, Masachika still couldn’t help but feel a strong reflexive sense of aversion to relying on Yuusho. He couldn’t deny the feeling of not wanting to expose someone as dignified as Alisa to someone like that.

And in the first place, getting involved with him now’s nothing but a risk if we’re thinking ’bout the election here… His awful reputation’s definitely dragging down our support if he ends up cooperating with our camp. Hmmmmm~

Seeing Masachika stuck in indecision after turning over every possible angle, Alisa could only shrug.

“Alright. I’ll go talk to him first alone.”

“Huh?”

“The two of you seem to have this heavy history, and you being there means he might not be able to stay calm either.”

“No, that’s…” Masachika instinctively tried to refute her words, only to trail off in the end.

But still, letting Alisa and Yuusho meet one-on-one was the last thing Masachika could accept.

Then again, setting aside all that emotion, thinking about it rationally made Alisa objectively correct: they should hear Yuusho out.

In that case, Masachika’s own conclusion was already set…

“Nnghhh~,” he squirmed. “Fine! But I’m coming too.”

“Eh? But like I said, you being there means he’ll—”

“I’ll leave the talking to you. I’ll just listen in from the back.”

“What, are you that worried about leaving it to me?” Alisa sulked with a displeased tone, prompting Masachika to shake his head.

“No, it’s not that I’m not confident with leaving it to you… I’m worried because I don’t know what he might do.”

“He’s not going to do anything, is he…?”

“No, no… No way he won’t,” Masachika immediately denied with a tone as if it were the most obvious thing in the world. “This is the guy who caused that whole mess at the cultural festival, y’know? It’s better to stay on your guard, ain’t it?”

“……”

“I see what you’re trying to say, but…” yet Alisa could only tilt her head, unconvinced.

“What?”

“Considering what happened at the cultural festival… Kiryuuin-san is the type who works from behind the scenes without dirtying his own hands, am I right? If we think about it that way, the chances of him doing something to me directly are pretty low, aren’t they…? There’s no reason for him to.”

“……”

Hearing Alisa’s calm and logical point, Masachika finally realized that the “rational judgment” he thought he was making was, in fact, driven purely by emotion.

Ah, I see… I was…

To put it simply, unable to stand the thought of leaving Alisa alone with Yuusho. The both of them alone in some room: just imagining that caused a thick fog of unease to spread deep within his chest.

No, that’s just… ’cause I’m worried about her. And because I just hate the damn guy. Ugh, but I guess that means I’m not one to talk, huh…?

Realizing that he was guilty of the same kind of thing he had just accused Yuusho of, namely how “the guy naturally has it out for Nonoa so there was no way they’d get an objective opinion,” Masachika reflected on himself with a heavy sigh.

Nevertheless, that didn’t change the fact that things that were hard to accept were simply hard to accept…

“…Oh well, just in case—”

“You’re overprotective, hm?” Alisa cut him off with a sigh mixed with exasperation and resignation at Masachika’s terse insistence on accompanying her, before putting on a faint sulkish expression as she then lightly pursed her lips while toying with a strand of her hair.

Seeing that, all Masachika could do was hesitate for a few seconds before averting his eyes.

“…I am worried, y’know?” he started off with that murmur. “Not about whether you can handle it… but about you.”

In face of the small fragment of his true feelings that Masachika let slip, Alisa’s eyes shot out wide. The fingers that played with her hair paused, and she stared at him as he looked away, his lips twitching awkwardly.

Quickly then casting her gaze downward…

“You are overprotective, aren’t you?” she repeated the same words, but with a different nuance this time as she started to fiddle with her hair again, her eyes darting all over the place.

【Not that I hate it though,】 she then added in a tiny whisper.

Ugh.

It had been a while since Alisa’s blunt murmurs of affection hit him square in the chest like that, and all Masachika could feel was his breath caught in that moment.

Still, pretending not to notice as she glanced at him over and over shyly, he forced a calm front.

“Then, that settles it. I’ll send Kiryuuin a message since thanks to the fact I’ve still got his contact from our time in the junior high student council; I’ll handle calling him over. As for the time and place…”

“…How about the student council room during lunch?”

“Mm… Sounds good. Let’s go with that, shall we?”

⋆⋅☆⋅⋆

“Hey, sorry ’bout that,” came an almost insincere voice. “Had a teacher stop me for a moment.”

““……””

It was now lunch break, and Yuusho had arrived at the student council room about five minutes later than the agreed time. Masachika greeted him with a glare, all the while Alisa shot him a look of 80% bewilderedness and 20% judgement.

Though he did technically offer an apology along with an excuse, his expression showed no remorse at all, completely at odds with his words.

Maybe he showed up late out of spite for calling him here so suddenly?

“Your baldness is spreading again, ain’t it?” Masachika lobbed that question straight at him, as if to substitute his criticism of how tardy he was.

“…It’s all Sumire-neesan’s choice, okay?” Yuusho explained after making a face akin to swallowing something unpleasant. “I have to keep my head shaved for at least the rest of the year.”

“Ahhh, so you’re getting it shaved regularly, huh? No wonder the patchy spots of hair keep shifting about a bit. Ain’t got a clue to how you’re shavin’ it here,” Masachika shrugged, earning a shot of unspoken protest from Yuusho before the latter composed himself.

“So then? What do you want?” Yuusho snapped in a slightly curt tone, throwing the two a suave side-glance that dripped with pretension.

“I’m just the messenger here,” Masachika responded by flicking his gaze toward Alisa with a dismissive gesture. “The one who wants to talk’s my partner here.”

Having said that, Masachika folded his arms as he leaned his back against the wall, making it clear that he intended to simply watch. As Yuusho responded with a slight shrug, Alisa stepped forward.

“Nice to meet you… I suppose that’s appropriate since it’s our first proper meeting, Kiryuuin-san?”

“Ahhh, that’s right,” Yuusho lifted his chin with an insufferably arrogant gesture. “Is calling you Kujou-san alright here?”

“Yes, ” Alisa responded while maintaining her serious expression. “I’d like you to be frank with me: what do you mean when you say that Miyamae-san is plotting something for the upcoming student assembly concerning the piano and light music clubs?”

Faced with her question, Yuusho tilted his head lightly before casting a quick glance toward Masachika.

“You hear that from Kuze?” he then spoke in a needlessly self-important tone. “Oh well, he’s the one who refused to listen to me at all, though~”

A blatant jab, one Masachika couldn’t help but twist his mouth over, with Alisa also frowning in tow.

“Isn’t it only natural that he wouldn’t want to listen if that’s the tone you take?” she pointed out clearly.

Her exceedingly straightforward remark made Yuusho’s eyes widen in surprise, and he instinctively ran his right hand through his hair as if dispirited… only to realize that there wasn’t any to grab at in the first place, letting his shoulders droop a little sadly.

“That’s true, I was clearly a bit rude. I apologize,” he then bowed his head honestly.

This time, it was Masachika who widened his eyes in surprise.

With Yuusho not saying anything more on that point, he passively dropped his theatrical demeanor and looked straight at Alisa.

“So, this is about Miyamae, was it? It’s simple enough. The whole matter clearly screams that someone’s malice is at work.”

“…Specifically?” Alisa probed, prompting Yuusho to snap his index finger upright as he continued.

“First, the fact our vice president’s trying to recklessly convene a student assembly. Given her personality, she’d normally try to persuade the light music club before ever resorting to something like this. Unless, of course, someone talked her into it, hm?”

“I see… and the next?”

Prompted, Yuusho then raised his middle finger alongside his index.

“Negative chatter about the piano club has been heating up again out of nowhere. For gossip that had been finally calming down to flare up again now? I can only guess that someone’s obviously stirring the pot.”

Having said that, he then lightly spread his arms and shrugged.

“Then, you’ve got the whole origin of this matter lying with none other than the light music club: the club Miyamae belongs to… And, well, the rest’s just my intuition.”

“Your intuition…” Alisa softly repeated his words, frowning for a while in thought. “…In other words, you mean you’re convinced this student assembly is all Nonoa-san’s doing, based on your own experience of being up against her back in junior high, right?”

“Well, that’s about it?” Yuusho confirmed. “Judging from how you’re acting, it looks like you’ve happened to get some solid information from someone other than me, huh now?”

“…Something like that.”

Though slipping past Yuusho’s own probing with ease, Alisa still wore a difficult expression as she deliberated.

“If you’re sitting there and wondering, ‘why would Miyamae do such a thing~?’, it’s pointless,” Yuusho shrugged and said. “That woman acts when she decides to act. Trying to analyze her reasoning using ordinary standards or common sense is utterly meaningless.”

His words pushed Alisa’s eyes to waver as she looked toward Masachika. Her look held a desperate desire for denial, and yet… all Masachika did was merely lower his own gaze slightly, offering Yuusho a form of reluctant agreement.

“!”

Precisely reading Masachika’s intent, Alisa clenched her teeth sharply and lowered her face.

“Alya…” Masachika muttered.

He stepped away from the wall to stand beside his partner as he saw her struggling. But just as he hesitantly reached out to place a hand on her shoulder, Alisa suddenly snapped her head up and looked straight at Yuusho.

“So then. Assuming Nonoa-san is plotting something, what exactly do you intend to do about it?”

“Stop her, obviously. The piano club’s survival is at stake here. And besides, the idea of letting that woman have her way puts a bad taste in my mouth.”

“How do you intend to specifically? You don’t actually know what Nonoa-san is planning either, do you?”

“I unfortunately have no obligation to be that frank with you, do I?” Yuusho turned his face away, refusing to answer this time.

“Then let’s make a deal, shall we?” Alisa offered, smoothly shifting from a position of questioning to that of negotiation as if she expected his response. “If you tell us your plan, I’ll share the info we’ve gathered. And if you’re intending to do something during the student assembly, then I’ll offer certain arrangements as a member of the hosting student council.”

Faced with her fluid words, Yuusho could only look over at her in mild surprise, staring directly at her face before letting out a wry smile.

“In other words, me refusing here means you might bar me from attending the student assembly altogether, is that it now?”

“Eh? No, that’s not—”

“Heh… You’d better learn to wield those sort of threats if you intend to become student council president someday~,” he then swapped the nature of his smile as he saw Alisa immediately let her gaze wander in distress, sweeping Masachika—who had quietly dropped his outreached hand—into view. “Sure. Regarding this student assembly, let’s form a united front, shall we?”

⋆⋅☆⋅⋆

“So, if push comes to shove, you’re saying you’ll provoke your former piano club members to bring the entire student assembly to a halt, right, Kiryuuin-san?”

“Sure, but that’s only possible if they’re moved in the first place, riiight~? And that… all depends on our vice prez, doesn’t it?”

“We should probably inform Prez and our vice president quietly then,” Alisa suggested. “Especially Sarashina-senpai. She’ll likely physically block a disruption onstage if we don’t lay the groundwork beforehand.”

“Ahaha, that’s easy to imagine alright…” Masachika uttered.

It was currently the afternoon after school. Following Yuusho’s insistence that they could never be sure which students on campus might be under Nonoa’s influence, the five of them—Masachika, Alisa, Yuki, Ayano, and Yuusho—had gathered at a karaoke parlor two stations away from school, sharing the information each of them had as they held a strategy meeting.

Given there were only a few days left before the student assembly would convene, they’d gathered in a rush. Still, with these five sitting face-to-face, the discussion moved quickly.

“I want to identify whatever tricks may be set in motion as much as possible… So could you wait until the last possible moment to intervene?” Alisa asked.

“Well, I want to expose Miyamae’s shenanigans as much as you do, so that’s what I’ll do,” Yuusho agreed. “But depending on how things go, I may move without waiting for a signal.”

“That’s fine with us.”

“Then I’ll head home on the day of,” Yuki concluded. “Masachika-kun will go to the wind ensemble clubroom, and we’ll all meet again afterward.”

“Yeah… Got it.”

With the meeting itself being wrapped up after just over thirty minutes, Masachika and the rest all let out small sighs as they sipped at their juices, all the while Yuusho suddenly queued up a song.

“…No, what’re you tryna sing for here?”

“Coming all the way here to karaoke and not singing at least one song’s pretty lame, isn’t it~?” he reasoned as he ignored Masachika’s lazy stare, adjusting the volume before standing up and beginning to sing in English. “Wow…..So jeallyyyy.”

A Western song too… Damn, he’s insanely good at it as well.

Letting out a small, exasperated sigh in the face of an utter narcissist enjoying himself alone, Masachika confirmed that Yuusho’s attention was fully fixed on the karaoke screen before turning to Ayano.

“So… you doing okay, Ayano?” he asked, with the girl who had, as always, erased her presence and blended into the air, jumping lightly at his question before tilting her head.

“…I am not experiencing any particular physical discomfort,” she stated, keeping her ever so formal tone.

“No, that’s not what I meant… Like, doing something you’re not used to, like spying? I was just wondering if you were holding up mentally here,” Masachika explained, yet he regretted asking something so foolish the moment he did.

There was no way she was okay. No matter how distant this childhood friend of his was from Nonoa, the very act of tricking someone and getting information out of them like that was something even she would feel hurt over.

And yet…

“There is no problem,” Ayano spoke. “I was merely driven by a sense of duty for a task that only I could accomplish.”

“……”

Her emotionless tone gave no insight to any of her true feelings. Glancing at his sister and seeing her raise her shoulders with a “it can’t be helped” gesture, Masachika chose not to press further.

Oh well, I’ll make sure to properly thank her once this is all over, he instead conveyed to Yuki with his eyes.

Yeah, that’s right, she silently replied with her own before picking up the remote. “Well then, since we’re already here, why don’t we sing a little too? But really… Kiryuuin-san’s actually good at singing…”

“The way he sings with that whole full of himself act really gets under my skin, though.”

“Eh? We’re singing now? Does that mean me too?” Alisa asked.

“Of course, it only really starts when our diva sings here.”

“Who’re you calling a diva… Geez.”

“I’m for some reason getting a li’l hungry here too; should we just get dinner here while we’re at it?”

“Ah~, sounds good. Let’s do that.”

And so, the five of them ended up enjoying a karaoke sesh for about an hour while having dinner before finally parting ways.

⋆⋅☆⋅⋆

“Right then, I’ll take a taxi home.”

“Okay then, see you tomorrow.”

“Thank you all for today. Please be careful on your way home.”

“Mm-hmm.”

“See you tomorrow.”

After watching Yuusho head to the main street and Yuki and Ayano get into the Suou family car, Masachika turned to Alisa.

“Right then, we should head back too,” he suggested.

“Yes.”

But as the two began walking side by side toward the station, Alisa suddenly let a small smile slip, making him blink in surprise.

“Alya? What’s up?”

“Ah, mm…” she shook her head a little sheepishly, probably not even fully conscious that she had smiled, pausing for a moment before speaking. “Um, hearing that Nonoa-san was trying to set up a trap for me had made me really uneasy, but… being able to work with Yuki-san and Ayano-san about it makes me feel relieved, I guess.”

Her thoughts seemed to settle all the more as she talked, and Alisa continued with a gentle smile.

“As for me, I do want to become student council president, and I absolutely don’t want to lose to Yuki-san… But at the same time, I guess it’s also true that I never really want to fight if I could help it.”

“Hmm…”

Though it was only temporary, Alisa appeared to be happy that she was cooperating with someone she considered both a rival and a friend. It was something that Masachika felt like agreeing with as well, almost responding with a calm nod.

“Yeah, true,” he wanted to say, however…

“…Hate to rain on your parade here, but you really shouldn’t be letting your guard down too much, y’know?”

“Hm? Wh-why?” Alisa blinked repeatedly as she turned toward him, caught off guard by his unexpected warning.

Looking away from her gaze, Masachika could only face forward as he spoke slowly.

“It’s true: we’ve decided to work together to deal with whatever Nonoa seems to be plotting up, but… that doesn’t make us allies. No, we’re still rivals at the core even with this whole thing. Yuki understands that too.”

“What… do you mean?”

“I mean…”

And with that, time returns to the day of the student assembly.

“Oh my, oh my… What a most distinguished gathering we have here,” Nonoa called out in a voice tinged with unmistakable mockery, greeting Masachika, Alisa, Yuki, and Yuusho as they stepped into the classroom at night.

Her expression was clearly one of delight, her eyes sparkling with glee as she faced the five of them wearing grim looks.

Normally, seeing a beautiful girl with such a look in her eyes would make just about anyone feel a fond warmth… Yet, when it came to Nonoa, it was an entirely different story.

“““““!”””””

What the five felt upon seeing her instead was a skin-prickling chill, a feeling that anyone who actually looked into her brown eyes at this moment would be forced to share.

True, they were vividly shining with life. And yet, because of that, her pupils stood out all the more starkly, as if they’d been gouged out and filled with a flat, uniform black, making it all the more eerie. It was akin to confronting an unknown creature disguised in the skin of a human… That kind of indescribably unsettling feeling.

“Phew… Told you, didn’t I, Kuze? That you should seriously think twice of making that your ally,” Yuusho sneered as he shook his head theatrically, whether it was his usual bravado or simply a quick attempt to recover his composure.

“……”

Masachika said nothing in response. Or perhaps, he couldn’t.

“That’s my line, y’know~?” Nonoa, the very person who’d just been dismissed so bluntly as “that,” reacted instead. “What’re you doing over there acting like one of the gang, Junyuushou-chan~?”

“Not saying I’m their ally or anything. It’s just it looked like you were dragging the piano club through something shady, weren’t you now? So I’m merely just cooperating temporarily to crush that li’l scheme of yours.”

“I was the one who brought him in,” Alisa stepped forward as she said that.

Nonoa could only widen her eyes in brief surprise in response, before bursting out into laughter while looking as if she were enjoying herself from the bottom of her heart.

“Ohoho~?” That’s how it is, hmm~? Welp, guess Kuzecchi wouldn’t willingly try to team up with Yuusho anyway~,” she speculated while shooting a sidelong glance at Masachika, whose mouth twisted in its corner as she hit the mark dead on, before resuming her analysis with a matter-of-fact tone. “So basically, knowing that someone was settin’ things up, Alissa here still went ahead and attended the student assembly all on her own, without a care in the world, ’cause she had Yuushou’s table-flip as insurance. You prepared a way to forcibly shut down the whole thing in advance, and purposefully dove headfirst into the trap to figure out who was plotting what.”

Laying out her deductions one after another as if they were mere idle musings, Nonoa then shifted her gaze to Alisa, who in turn wore a stern expression.

“Then, when Vice-Prez-san started screaming all about fraud, you more or less grasped the whole setup… and deliberately called for a revote to pinpoint the culprit. That’s bold, riiiight~?” she stated with a cheerful smile playing at her lips, clapping her hands as if to praise Alisa’s valiant effort.

*Clap clap, clap, clap, clap.*

The sound of her applause echoed, somehow chilling in the silent classroom.

An empty applause that no one else joined in on… As it came to its end, Nonoa kept her hands clasped together with a soft thud, letting her smile drop away in an instant before raising one eyebrow and lightly spreading both her arms.

“So,” she called out. “What’s this?”

This being the current situation: pressed by the five of them with Alisa at the forefront.

“I’ve got absolutely no idea what’s the cause of all this. I don’t understand why you’re all here doing this to me.”

That was the attitude she projected, an attitude so brazen that it seemed nothing but insolent to Masachika and the others. Even Alisa and Yuki couldn’t help but furrow their brows in response.

“Nonoa-san, you appeared to have known that something would happen even before it was decided that a student assembly was to be convened, and you hinted as much to Ayano,” the latter stated, being the first to speak as she maintained her refined ladylike smile. “Why was that?”

“Well look, I’ve got loads of acquaintances, right? Kiiinda heard some rumors from them, like there was some shaaaady stuff goin’ on to target Alissa~. I was actually originally planning to warn Kuzecchi and her ’bout it, y’know~? …But, you see, I’d already said I’d side with Ayanono, didn’t Iiii~? Welp… was never expecting her to pass all that info to you and Alissa, though.”

Nonoa had simply pretended to play out the role of a well-meaning informant. It was a smooth explanation lacking any hesitation, spun with such a carefree smile, and sounded so natural that anyone who didn’t know her true nature would instinctively have the thought, “Oh, I-I see how it is,” spring into mind as they easily found themselves accepting it outright.

However…

“““““……”””””

There was, of course, not a single person present who truly bought that story. None at all, and yet… there also wasn’t any concrete proof to decisively brand it as a lie either.

Following the body and baggage inspection of those who’d attended the student assembly earlier, eight perpetrators involved in manipulating the voting results had already been apprehended. Yet, during such an inspection, Nonoa had been cleared. No testimony linking her to any crime could be obtained from those caught as well. The only thing the eight of them—alongside Aoi, the piano club’s vice president—had said unanimously was that they had been egged on by an unfamiliar female student. A student whose physique and appearance didn’t match Nonoa’s at all… What was more, Ayano herself had not been able to obtain any incriminating statement of admission from Nonoa up until this point either. Despite never realizing that she was only pretending to be compliant while plotting otherwise, Nonoa had maneuvered with such care to ensure that she would never be allowed to be pinned down by her own words.

“I mean, it sounded like Ayanono wanted Kuzecchi and you to get along, right, Yukki?” Nonoa nonchalantly explained. “So, just to make sure that neither of you would’ve gotten caught up in any plot targeting Alissa by any chance, I went out of my way to make sure that the two of you didn’t participate in the student assembly.”

“Then what was with pulling the strings to get Ayano and Alya-san to handle the votes?” Yuki pressed further.

“There’s nothing really deep ’bout it, though? If Alissa was being targeted, then Ayanono—who knew that much—might as well stay with her. Being close together means she’d notice right away if something actually happened, right? So, in the event that Alissa actually ends up in a pinch, wouldn’t the question of whether to help her or not be up to Ayanono? Something like that?”

“In that case, wasn’t there no need to designate them as vote counters?”

“Welp, maybe you’re right… But counting the votes means you’d always be up on the stage, and therefore be able to see the whole venue, right?” Nonoa reasoned. “On the flip side, given it makes you so clearly visible from where the audience is sitting, it’d be harder for the culprits to make their move. It was simply a placement I thought worked the best both offensively and defensively. I did at least try to be considerate in my own way, y’know~?”

“……”

Smoothly delivered excuses with a slack, easy smile still on her face. It was a moment where Yuki could only maintain her refined smile, with lips sealed shut, in response to. She had probably judged that continuing to press the issue head-on like this would be like pushing water uphill. Masachika, too, thought that Nonoa’s excuses, though impressively bold, were flawless. So flawless, in fact, that they looped back to bordering on suspicion.

Then, maybe because she had sensed that Yuki’s offensive had now stalled, Nonoa let her expression drain away as she turned her gaze toward Ayano.

“By the way, when did you start leaking all this, Ayanono?” she questioned, leaning her upper body sharply to her left. “I was helping you out because you said you wanted Kuzecchi and Yukki to get along, you know~? Was that all a lie then?”

“…I had already received warnings from Yuki-sama and Masachika-sama to be cautious around you, Nonoa-san,” Ayano opened her mouth to explain after slowly blinking in response.

She spoke with a calm and careful tone, as if she were organizing her own thoughts.

“That you are exceptional when it comes to manipulating others, a genius when it comes to controlling hearts… And that you have been able to carry out numerous covert schemes until now with such talent. That is precisely why… that day, on the stairs, when you closed your distance with me…” she continued, recalling back to the time on that emergency staircase when Nonoa had pressed her with such eloquent words, urging her into self-disclosure despite them being almost complete strangers back then, “…I became wary. I had suspected that you might have some sort of plot at play when you had approached me for that reason… It was precisely why I decided to deliberately show an opening myself to observe your reaction, Nonoa-san.”

Nonoa could only narrow her eyes slightly at her words. Deliberately revealing a weakness to slip into another person’s inner circle? That was exactly the method Nonoa herself had used on Masachika prior to approaching Ayano.

So I ended up being caught by the very method I used myself, huh…? she lamented. That was pretty careless of me, wasn’t iiit~?

It was a realization that induced a strange amusement inside of her, one that made her want to applaud even as she let a wry smile creep across her face. Even so, she shook her head side to side with an aggrieved look.

“That hurts, y’know…? To think that both Kuzecchi and Yukki would look at me like that. And you too, Ayanono. All I did was listen to you sincerely while giving advice,” Nonoa spoke as if she were the victim, spitting out words that grated on the nerves.

“Do you really think such an excuse will pass?” Yuki asked.

“I don’t, y’know? But if it’s the truth, there’s nothing that could be done, could it?”

Even to her question, one that carried a subtle heightened pressure, Nonoa simply replied with a calm, feigned air of innocence.

At this, Alisa finally opened her mouth with a frustrated huff, unable to hold back any longer as she—

“!”

Yet even faster than that, Masachika stepped forward to grab her hand, stopping her from speaking. Seeing his partner turn to him in surprise, Masachika signaled with his eyes and a quick flick at her palm that he would handle this himself.

Adding to this, he directed his gaze toward Ayano’s skirt pocket, causing Alisa to fall silent with an albeit startled expression.

Good, good… Looks like she’s calmed down.

Relieved that he’d managed to stop Alisa from saying something rash, Masachika let out a quiet sigh of relief.

Facing Nonoa here was unexpected even for Masachika. Because of that, he hadn’t had the privilege of discussing with Alisa beforehand to coordinate how they should handle the present debacle… Still, that didn’t change the fact that they had already strategized how to handle such general situations like this before.

As I thought, making sure we’re aligned in our course of action ahead of time really does matter. Right, everything’s gone according to plan up to this point. From here on, it’s all about whether I can steer this convo to the exact point we’re heading for. That’s where it counts.

It was for that reason that he had to be careful with every single word from here on.

The whole reason we’ve been able to crush Nonoa’s scheme and corner her this far has been entirely because of Alya. She’s got Kiryuuin on our side and caught the other perpetrators, and we’ve gotten this far thanks to that… But it’s all ’bout the battle of the words from here on out, and Alya’s got practically no experience with this kinda verbal deception. Taking on Nonoa and whoever’s out there like that would be too much for her.

So from here on, Masachika wanted her to leave it to him, pouring all that intent into his gaze as he stared straight into her eyes. With that, Alisa lowered her gaze slightly before nodding and stepping half a pace back.

“Do your best,” came his partner’s words, brimming with nothing but trust, flowing into him through the contact of their hands.

Drawing courage from that, Masachika switched his mindset into battle mode once more.

Alright… This is where it all counts, me, he addressed himself, steeling his resolve as he fixed his gaze on Nonoa, something she seemed to sense as she turned her eyes toward him as well, her lips curving into an amused grin.

“So, what about it, Kuzecchi?” A question tinged with provocation then came from those lips. “Will you believe me?””

“……”

Meeting Nonoa’s probing stare with a stern one of his own, Masachika scratched at the back of his neck with his left hand.

“Yeah, I believe you,” he answered. “Oh well, can’t be helped if that’s how it is.”

His words prompted Ayano to widen her eyes as she looked toward him. Meanwhile, Nonoa’s smile deepened in satisfaction.

Her question was simply her just extending a hand toward Masachika, after all. A hand that he had firmly taken.

Welp, of course you had no choice but to do that, did you now, Kuzecchi~? Nonoa thought, full of certainty after hearing Masachika’s reply.

She was now sure that this conversation was, at this very moment, being recorded, most likely by Ayano. And that Masachika had no intention of cutting Nonoa loose.

Why of course, right~? Because if you won’t stand a chance in the election if you cut me off, would you~?

Yes, Nonoa understood. She understood that in this situation, right here and now, Masachika and Alisa had no choice but to protect her.

Her popularity was extraordinarily high within this school, after all. If her betrayal were to come to light, Masachika and Alisa would completely lose the supporters who stood behind her. On top of that, they had boldly declared to the entire student body that they would be working together as fellow student council officers if they were to be elected back during the closing ceremony of the first semester. An internal strife erupting less than half a year later would inevitably mean that people would say that they lacked the ability to bring others together.

Even if, hypothetically, all the evidence of my betrayal were to come out, proving that I was entirely at fault beyond doubt, we’d still get a “Looks like they’re fighting themselves anyway, so let’s just play it safe and vote for Suou-san” type of situation. If it’ll end up being that way, then Kuzecchi’s best bet is to cover up the very fact of betrayal itself.

In short, in this place and moment, Masachika and Alisa could not be Nonoa’s enemies. Yet, the instant she became certain of that, Nonoa felt her excitement rapidly drain away.

Ahhh… That’s boring, right?

It was essentially all just a dead rubber from here on out. All that would unfold would just be Yuki and Yuusho’s persistence in trying to squeeze some sort of definite statement out of her, while Masachika would keep them in check. It basically just required Nonoa to be careful to not slip up, a casual situation where she could just dodge and weave obstacles nonchalantly. Having read that far ahead, her interest waned, and she turned her eyes to the wall clock in the classroom.

Yet, however…

“But to begin with, you’re fundamentally lazy: you’ve got no reason to go through all that trouble to backstab us,” Masachika conjectured. “The only scenario that I can think of is that Sayaka’s still actually aiming to be president and told you to set us up.”

At his words, Nonoa froze for an instant before turning her gaze back.

There, she saw Masachika’s mouth curved into a loose, casual smile. “Oh well, it probably ain’t like that, though…” it seemed to say, yet his eyes fostered a keen, icy light. It was something that Nonoa understood with complete clarity: a clear threat.

Haaah~, so that’s how you’re comin’ at me.

In other words, Nonoa committing any further acts of betrayal aimed at causing harm to the Masachika-Alisa pair would only result in Sayaka being made to shoulder the responsibility. That was essentially what Masachika was saying. It was, without any question, a threat with the full understanding of Nonoa’s weak spot.

So you’re still laying down the law while protecting me, huh? Nonoa lamented. Maybe it’s still too early to let my guard down, after all?

Revising her assessment that Masachika was no longer an enemy, Nonoa shifted her thoughts back into gear.

But y’know…? That threat doesn’t really exist, Kuzecchi. The oh-so-good-natured Kuzecchi pinning the stigma of being a traitor on an innocent Sayacchi? You wouldn’t be able to do that, would you? she mused, giving a dispassionate analysis of the situation with a cool head.

And yet, as if he’d seen straight through her thoughts, Masachika turned toward Yuusho.

“Hey, Kiryuuin,” he called out. “You think so too, don’t ya?”

“…Yeah, you’re right. Miyamae denying it here would just surely mean she’s protecting Taniyama. After all, she did take the blame to shield her at that debate during the first semester as well, amirite?” Yuusho answered, giving a theatrically exaggerated shrug, making Nonoa narrow her eyes slightly.

Ah… Yeah, Yuushou’s definitely happy to slap that kinda stigma onto Sayacchi if it’s him we’re talking about. Even if Kuzecchi tries to stop him…

She understood now. This really did work… as a threat.

No way… To think that Yuushou would end up playing the joker here…

He was already a loser whose status within the school had fallen as far as it could, shunned by every member of the current student council. Nonoa had been keeping an eye on his movements, given that he’s the head of the very piano club that had formed the basis for her whole scheme to start with, but in all honesty, she hadn’t been particularly wary of him at all.

And yet, to think your plans have been crushed by ol’ loser-chan over here, going all the way to set your fate in stone, hm…? Yuusho conveyed as much with a provocative jerk of his chin, as if he’d read her thoughts.

It was the type of gesture that should have been irritating beyond measure, and yet… it felt amusing to Nonoa. It was as though the excitement that had once cooled was flaring back up with a sudden whoosh.

Ahhhh… How nice, she thought. That’s right, guess I should play along here?

Letting that inner amusement rise to her cheeks, Nonoa flashed a grin so bright that it almost seemed fake.

“Of coooourse, isn’t there just noooo way I’d betray Kuzecchi and Alissa?” she mused. “I mean, suuure~, I might’ve if Sayacchi had told me to, but… she would never ask for such a thing, would she?”

“Welp, that’s true. I naturally believe that too,” Masachika answered, returning an equally dubious-looking cheerful smile as he continued to scratch the back of his neck with his left hand.

Fully aware that neither was saying what they truly meant, the two exchanged friendly grins all the same.

“But it’s truuue~. It’s true I sided with Ayanono instead of giving you two the warnings I should have; I swear I’ll make up for it sometime soon, okaaaay~?”

“That so? That’d be a great help. Just make sure to report back to us and communicate properly when the time comes, alright?”

The two continued to maintain their outwardly amicable demeanors as they kept up with the quiet sparring beneath the surface… At least, until Yuki suddenly jumped in between them.

“Nonoa-san,” she called out. “Hand over who incited both the piano club’s vice president and the actual perpetrators, and we promise we won’t go after you any further. What do you say?”

Her proposal, casually tossed out, caught Nonoa completely off guard. A question posed in the form of an offer, one where showing even an ounce of hesitation would mean defeat.

“Hmm~? Sorry, but I don’t really get what you’re talkin’ about here, Yukki,” yet she replied without even the slightest of pauses.

“……”

Once again unable to extract a straight answer, Yuki lightly narrowed her gaze as she gave off a subtle air of frustration, as if she were clicking her tongue inwardly.

And then, at that moment…

“H-how…?”

A voice perked up, unexpected not only for Yuki and Nonoa… but for Masachika as well.

“?”

“H-how!? How! How can you be so calm about this!?” cried a thin, squeezed out voice, belonging to none other than Ayano as she stood diagonally behind Yuki.

“I-it’s fine if it’s m-me. But Alisa and… Masachika-sama… th-they are, to you, Nonoa-san, f-friends, are they not!?” Ayano continued to shout with trembling lips, clenching her skirt tightly as the astonished gazes of everyone present turned toward her. “A-and yet you… b-betrayed th-those two, you… you—!”

Her words seemed to spill from the deepest settings of her heart before her head could even catch up. Her throat, her chest, her fists, her entire body shook violently as she desperately forced out her words with a tongue that wouldn’t cooperate. It was a raw display of passion from Ayano that even Masachika and Yuki rarely ever saw. She looked as though she might hyperventilate at any moment…

So as Yuki turned back, she pulled her into a tight embrace.

“Thank you, Ayano. It’s okay now. It’s really all okay now.”

“Y-Yuki… sama…”

As she gently stroked Ayano’s head, the tension gradually drained from her stiff body, and her breathing started to settle little by little. In front of her, Masachika and Alisa stepped forward, positioning themselves to block Nonoa from her view.

“Thanks, Ayano.”

“Thank you, Ayano-san. For getting angry on our behalf.”

With the former gently patting her head just as his sister had, and the latter giving a gentle, considerate smile, Ayano finally slowly took a deep breath as she lowered her gaze.

“…Masachika-kun, Alya-san,” Yuki said. “We will be heading home a little ahead of you two.”

“Yeah… Take care of Ayano.”

“Yes. Then, to you too, Kiryuuin-san,” she then addressed Yuusho, leaving only those words behind before exiting the classroom while holding Ayano close.

After watching their retreating figures, Masachika turned to Yuusho.

“You really saved us today, Kiryuuin. Thank you,” he expressed his attitude, bowing toward him.

“Oh…? Y-yeah…”

“But sorry, could you head home for now?” Masachika continued, unfazed by Yuusho, who had blinked repeatedly with a surprised expression on his face, clearly caught off guard. “I want to talk with Nonoa, just Alya and me.”

“Ah, mm…”

And with that, Yuusho also left the classroom, albeit looking unusually shaken as he nodded with an uncharacteristic obedience.

So, with only the three of them remaining, Masachika and Alisa faced Nonoa once again.

“So then, why did you end up backstabbing us?” the former asked her bluntly, discarding his manufactured, plastered-on smile.

“What’s gotten into you all a sudden, Kuzecchi?” Yet Nonoa merely deflected his question with the mere tilt of her head, her bright smile unchanged. “You said you’d believe me.”

“…Is that right? So you really have no intention of admitting it, hm?” Masachika spoke, inwardly clicking his tongue when faced with Nonoa as she continued her transparent act, unwilling to let her guard down or show a single opening.

Tsk. So you ain’t gonna slip up that easily, huh…? Masachika mused, scratching his head roughly with his right hand and dropping his gaze downward before continuing.

“Hey, Nonoa. Who was the female student that tried to set Alya up?”

“Geeez~, I told you. I don’t get what you’re talking about.”

“Oh, you don’t get what I’m talking about? You’re really serious?”

“Mm, not a clue~” Nonoa answered in an offhand tone, spreading both hands lightly as she did… only for Masachika to let out a small chuckle.

“Yeah, figures,” he commented. “Yuki did ask you something similar earlier, yet you kept feigning your ignorance of it, after all.”

“Right, right~,” Nonoa agreed, recalling how Yuki had pressed her. “I really wish you’d cut it out alrea—”

“There we go, knew you’d slip up eventually.”

Nonoa’s smile vanished in an instant.

“You don’t get what I’m talking about?” Masachika continued, staring straight at Nonoa, who had, in turn, gone utterly blank-faced in an instant. “What a strange thing to say. Y’know, wouldn’t you think that the first person that should’ve come to mind with the description, ‘the female student that tried to set Alya up,’ be the girl who’d confronted her from the audience back during the student assembly?”

In other words, one of the perpetrators who had manipulated the colors of the balls they had used to cast their vote. The very girl who was the first to denounce Alisa. Perhaps recalling her existence, Nonoa’s eyes widened just slightly.

“If you truly knew nothing, then you would’ve answered my question with something like, say, I don’t know, ‘She was Yuki’s classmate,’ or, ‘I don’t know who she is.’ And yet, when you heard my words, ‘the female student that tried to set Alya up,’ who you instantly thought of was the female student who incited those eight perpetrators and the piano club’s vice president. Someone that you, who definitely really knows nothing here, shouldn’t even know about. That’s what you told me, right? That you, quote-unquote, don’t get what I’m talking about, hm?”

Saying that much, Masachika then showed Nonoa the still-recording voice recorder he’d pulled out from his pocket, causing her eyes to shoot open even wider…

“Well, you see,” she spoke, letting out a soft chuckle. “Yuki had mentioned that there was such a person, didn’t she?”

“That’s absolutely true. But what she specifically asked was who incited them. She never once mentioned a female student.”

“You say that, but it’s still within the realm of worldplay, if anything… Isn’t that a li’l too weak as proof of betrayal?”

“It’d be real nice if that argument works on Sayaka too,” Masachika retorted wittily, causing the cracks to finally spread across Nonoa’s plastic smile as a hint of madness peeked through from within.

“…How interesting. You really are an interesting one, aren’t you, Kuzzechiii~? You’re about the only person who can corner me head-on like this.”

Her eyes gleamed brightly as she stared ahead, and she donned an expression that belonged to someone itching to lick their lips at any moment. It was a presence that would engraft an unconditional sense of danger to any ordinary person.

“What… are you?” Alya finally raised her voice as she faced such a sight. “What is it… that you want?”

It was a question that had slipped out almost involuntarily, prompting Nonoa to turn toward her this time, her eerie smile still firmly in place.

“Hmm~? What am I, huuuh…? To be honest, I don’t really understand myself all that well either… Ah, but maybe I’ve figured it out just a little today,” she murmured, before tearing her mouth into a wide grin as she threw both her arms open and looked up toward the ceiling.

“I want to witness the unexpected!”

Clenching both her hands tightly, as though she was grasping for something, Nonoa let out a sick laugh.

“Things that go beyond my expectations! Things that overturn them! All for me! That’s what I want to see!”

It was the first time Masachika had witnessed such a raw outpouring of pure desire from Nonoa. It was something so animalistic, a craving that was so unfiltered. Something that he could only frown at.

“So for that, you’d betray a friend or trick an innocent classmate. And you wouldn’t care, huh?”

“…Well, I never expected you to understand,” Nonoa responded, her head snapping back forward as her feverish madness cooled in an instant. “I don’t even understand why I feel this way myself.”

“I can’t say I can understand it too, but… I don’t think that’s a reason to deny it either,” a voice, which sounded as though it cast even herself aside, then responded to her remark.

It belonged to none other than Alisa.

“Just like how I always want to aim higher, you want to see the unexpected. That’s all there is to it, isn’t it?” she continued, looking straight at Nonoa all the while Masachika—and she as well—stared at her with eyes wide. “I’ve come to learn that all kinds of people live all kinds of lives ever since I enrolled in this school. And that there’s just no such superiority or inferiority among said ways of living either.”

Her words, backed by an undeniable sense of conviction, carried tremendous weight. A weight strong enough to naturally convince anyone listening that they were not spoken lightly. That they were not just mere words for show.

“Every way of living has its own merits and… there are just things that only someone living a specific life can see. So, regarding things I don’t understand, I’ve decided not to use their differences from myself as reasons to deny them. It’s what I’ve decided on. That’s why… I won’t deny you either. If that’s what gives you a reason to live then… I’ll accept it for what it is.”

A response that was neither affirmation nor rejection: acceptance. Something that Nonoa could only stare intently at Alisa over…

“How nice…” she murmured, breaking into a wide grin. “I think I might kinda like you, Alissa.”

“H-huh?”

“Mm-hmm, mm-hmm, that thought sounds gooood~. You were like that back at the student assembly earlier too, that was really great. I kinda wanna kiss you.”

“Uehh!? No, that’s…!” Alisa protested, instinctively taking a step back while Masachika shifted sideways to shield her.

Watching the both of them with clear amusement, Nonoa then spun around and turned her body toward the rear classroom door.

“Oh well, anyway… as long as you keep showing me things that exceed my expectations, I’ll proooperly cooperate with you two, ’kaaaay~?” she teased. “I’ll start stirrin’ things up if I get bored, though.”

“And we’ll make sure to give a response worthy of it if it comes to that.”

“Do as you liiike~. Oh, and go ahead if you wanna let Sayacchi hear this whole convo. Feel free~”

And with those parting words, maintaining her cheerful attitude to the very end, Nonoa left the classroom.

“Well that was something…” Masachika uttered after letting out a long breath and making sure she was gone, turning to Alisa. “Nice work. You okay?”

“Yes, thanks for your hard work too… But, ‘you okay’?” Alisa asked, confused with his sudden question.

“No, um… Seeing her true self was like that was a first for you, right? I was just wondering if it shook you up.”

Faced with Masachika’s concern, Alisa fell into serious thought.

“…I was surprised, that’s true,” she slowly opened her mouth after a short while, carefully picking her words as she went. “But as I said earlier, I don’t intend on denying who Nonoa-san is. If anything, I think that her showing her true nature—or rather… the core of who she is?—was a good thing.

A response that was not one of bravado, nor indulgence toward a friend, but a conclusion she’d reached after proper consideration. Something that Masachika felt a genuine respect for Alisa over.

“It’s amazing… that you’re able to think that way,” he sang his praise.

“W-well, I suppose part of it is because it makes it feel like I wasn’t really betrayed.”

“Ahhh, gotcha.”

True enough, the plot against them itself had been thwarted partway through, and Nonoa hadn’t directly done anything to Alisa herself. Maybe that was precisely why Alisa could still view Nonoa somewhat objectively.

“Well, besides that…? It was nothing compared to who Yuki-san truly is,” she commented.

“…Yeah, right~?” Masachika replied, only being able to stare off into the distance.

Thinking of his little sister—someone who was even closer to Alisa than Nonoa ever was, and someone whose gap between her public façade and true self surpassed that of Nonoa’s—Masachika cleared his throat lightly before pulling himself together.

“Oh well, glad you weren’t too shaken… It’s getting late anyway; let’s head home for today.”

“Yes… Okay.”

Then, without either of them taking the lead, the two began to walk, leaving the school building and strolling side by side as they headed home along the dark night road.

“So, what are we going to do? About that recording from earlier?” Alisa asked.

“Hmm… Let’s put it on hold for now. There’s no telling how Nonoa’s gonna react if Sayaka actually finds out about her backstabbing us and tries to stop her. Worst case scenario, she might just throw caution to the wind and openly turn against us… Relying on Sayaka has gotta be a last resort. We’ll keep it as some sorta deterrent against Nonoa for now.”

“I see… I suppose it’s fine if you say so.”

“…Mm,” Masachika nodded slightly, exhaling as he released all the tension that he had been holding onto.

And then, all at once, a deep fatigue washed over him.

Yeah, I really was on edge during that convo, wasn’t I…? No, sure, that’s part of it, but this is…

What he was feeling wasn’t just mental fatigue, but instead a murky, heavy feeling in his chest… Emotional fatigue.

Ah… That’s it.

It was from the outburst of raw emotion Ayano had shown earlier. The lingering image of his usually expressionless childhood friend like that weighed heavy on Masachika’s heart.

As for why she blew up back there… I’m partly to blame if you think ’bout it calmly, aren’t I?

At the very least, it was something that could have been avoided had Masachika not taken Nonoa’s side, instead joining Yuki in seriously condemning her. Ayano would have easily stayed as she always did if he’d done that, behind Masachika and Yuki as usual…

No, it was gonna happen sooner or later… huh? She’d been bottling it all up ever since she started spying on Nonoa, after all…

Even so, the fact remained that, despite Ayano putting such a burden on her heart to spy and warn Masachika and Alisa of danger, Masachika had still ended up repaying her kindness with what could only be described as an act of ingratitude.

We’d used her info to dodge Nonoa’s scheme, and yet when it actually came time to confront her, I ended up taking “her side” to stop it… Masachika lamented. That must’ve definitely looked like nothing but outright betrayal from Ayano’s perspective…

Still, Masachika had no regrets about how he had handled himself back then. With the upcoming election in mind, he believed he had handled the situation in the most optimal way possible, given the situation at hand as well. Still… it was also true that such relentlessly rational and calculating actions had caused Ayano to break down into such a fit.

Ugh… This makes me kinda… hate myself.

It couldn’t be helped, after all. They were opposing candidates. It was something Masachika understood on the logical level. He really did. And yet… right now, even making such attempts to justify it all made him feel even more unbearably detestable.

“Thanks, okay? For thinking things through deeply,” yet words of thanks came from beside him suddenly.

“Huh?”

They had caught him completely off guard, halting his thoughts. Turning to his side, he saw Alisa, still facing forward as she continued to speak slowly.

“If that was just me alone back there… I really might have just confronted Nonoa-san without thinking that far ahead, leaving nothing behind but distrust and friction before ending it all and breaking things off.”

“Yeah… Oh well, that straightforwardness of yours is one of your good points though, Alya.”

It was a straightforwardness that was always dazzling to Masachika… And yet, right now, that admiration hurted a little.

“But even so, I’m sure that that alone would’ve just let Nonoa-san continue with all that nonchalant dodging, and she wouldn’t have let us hear her true feelings,” Alisa opined. “The reason she showed us what she was really thinking was because you drew it out of the course of that conversation… So, thank you,” she then turned back to thank him, having walked a few steps ahead.

Masachika widened his eyes slightly in response. Meeting such a gaze head-on, Alisa could only widen hers as well.

“…What’s wrong?” she asked.

“Huh…?”

“You somehow… look like you’re in pain…”

“…Ah,” Masachika murmured, tugging the corner of his mouth up in a wry smile in response to her question. “It’s about Ayano… A li’l bit.”

“Ah…”

“As I thought… she really isn’t cut out for elections like this. Wait, I guess I’m the whole dang reason why she’s involved in all this in the first place, though…”

And part of why she made that face this time too…

“Masachika-kun…”

“…Really?” she squeaked, catching herself far too late. “Well… I suppose I don’t mind… if that’s the case? But even so…”

Unable to bring herself to finish her words, she brushed her hair back in an attempt to hide her embarrassment, all the while Masachika could only furrow his brows, his expression clouded with confusion as he tried to trace where her words were leading to.

Shooting a few sideway glances toward him, Alisa spoke again.

“If what you want is to dance together alone, like at the cultural festival’s after party… then I’m fine with that too, you know? I’m the one being escorted, after all. I’ll go along with your lead.”

Her words, declared so boldly, conveyed her absolute trust and willingness to fall right into his arms… It instantly blew away all the sense of inferiority that had wrapped its thorns around Masachika’s heart.

Yeah, she’s right, huh…? I can’t afford to be tormented by this stupid inferiority complex if she’s saying something like this. I really ain’t no man if I can’t hold my head high here, am I?

Feeling a surge of omnipotence coursing through his veins, Masachika felt his invincible mode reactivate once again.

“Thanks for having that much faith in me,” he shot her a fearless grin. “…But honestly, if anything, I actually feel like showing you off to everyone right now.”

“Oh my, is that so?” Alisa’s lips curved up into a provocative smirk. “Well then, let’s hold our heads high and give everyone something to look at, shall we?”

Even the sheer insolence in her tone was ridiculous. Masachika could only chuckle, throwing his hands up in defeat.

“Alrighty, shall we go, my princess?”

“Yes. Let’s, shall we?”

Hello, SunSunSun here, the original author. As I had also written in the afterword of Volume 8 of the manga adaptation, I, SunSunSun, quit my company job in August to become a full-time author. Wooooh! It reaaally ain’t exactly something I should be celebrating, though!!!

No, but all things considered, I guess I’d been a part-time author for about four and a half years, huh? Even I would call that a preeetty long time, wouldn’t I? So then, why did I keep this as just a side-gig for so long? I actually get asked that quite often, so I’ll answer it here: the reason was because I wanted to be prepared to be able to quit being a professional novelist at any time. That’s really how it was, you know? To put it more bluntly, it’s because I had neither the confidence or resolve to live the rest of my life as a novelist. I guess you’d get away with describing it like that, right? As I had written in the afterwords of Volumes 1 and 2, I was originally part of the whole “just enjoying Shousetsuka ni Narou” crowd, and never once actually thought that I’d be able to make my professional debut as a novelist.

So, embarrassingly enough, even when my debut had been set in stone, I actually had none of that whole “Alrighty, I’ll be making a livin’ solely on writing novels from here on out!” type of determination, you know? However, with Roshidere growing into a much bigger series that I could have ever imagined after, I unexpectedly found myself becoming an extremely busy author. But even so, that didn’t make me suddenly say things like, “Alright, guess I’ll go all in with being a full-time novelist, huh?” or anything… So that’s why, even though I was super swamped, I just couldn’t bring myself to quit my company job. In the end, what changed my mind was hearing that there were actually quite the number of authors and manga artists who went in full-time for a while, before then going back to being company employees during their forties and whatnot, you know? It meant that you didn;’t actually have to make a living through solely writing for the rest of your life just because you became a full-time author… Realizing that made it seem actually sort of obvious, and I thought, well, I guess maybe I don’t need to force myself to keep this double career way of living, huh? So, yes, in other words, I still don’t have the confidence or resolve to continue being a novelist for the rest of my life even now. Perhaps I’ll be back working as some company employee again in a few years from now, but for the time being, I think I’ll stick to writing Roshidere while consuming more material for creative input and the like—something that was pretty difficult to manage when I still had this whole double career thing. Hopefully I’ll be able to draw inspiration from all of that and even try writing a new series… That’s the sort of thing I’ve got in my mind right now, so I think I’ll try my best to work as a full-time and professional novelist for as long as I can.

Now then, I’ll leave my pointless ramblings about my own life at that. I’ve got an actual promotional announcement that I’ve been unusually asked to make, so let’s do that, shall we?
